summary.short: Swiss federal copyright statute (URG, 9 October 1992; in force 1 July 1993 per enactment note). Sets authors' and related-rights holders' exclusive rights, exceptions, protection terms, collecting society regulation, technical-measure protection, hosting duties and civil and criminal enforcement for works in Switzerland.
summary.long: The Swiss Federal Act on Copyright and Related Rights (URG) of 9 October 1992 sets out authors' exclusive rights in literary and artistic works (Arts. 9–16) and related rights of performers, phonogram producers and broadcasters (Arts. 33–39). It defines protected works (Art. 2), lists exceptions including private use (Art. 19), quotation (Art. 25), reproductions for scientific research (Art. 24d) and works made accessible to persons with disabilities (Art. 24c), and sets protection terms (Arts. 29–31). Collecting societies require authorisation from the Institut für geistiges Eigentum (IGE) (Arts. 41–43), and their tariffs are approved by an arbitration commission (Arts. 46, 55–59). The Act prohibits circumvention of effective technical measures and the making or sale of related devices (Art. 39a), protects rights-management information (Art. 39c), requires hosting operators to prevent repeated infringement under stated conditions (Art. 39d), and provides for civil remedies, criminal penalties and border measures against infringing goods (Arts. 61–77h). The enactment note gives 1 July 1993 as the date of entry into force.

notes: Consolidated text (Stand 1 July 2025) of the 1992 act. Relations are coded from in-text references and from amendment footnotes; no target is in the registry, so target_instrument_id is empty. Art. 84 gives 1 July 1993 as the entry-into-force date and Art. 74 Abs. 1 is printed as 1 January 1994. Art. 67 Abs. 2 and Art. 69 Abs. 2 end in an ellipsis where text was removed; Art. 77c Abs. 1 and 3 are repealed. Art. 65 is also changed by the ZPO (Fn. 63), and Art. 82 refers to the 1940 act repealed by Art. 79 lit. b.
